stored_text.note: official.pdf is the full Korean guideline (33 PDF pages) with a usable text layer. The cover (PDF page 1) is image-only; read from a rendering, it shows the title '인공지능 투명성 확보 가이드라인' with the logos of TTA (한국정보통신기술협회, Telecommunications Technology Association) and MSIT (과학기술정보통신부, Ministry of Science and ICT). secondary.html is the korea.kr press-release page: it holds the headline '과기정통부, 「인공지능 투명성 확보 가이드라인」 공개', the date 2026.01.21 and the attachment names, but not the press-release body.

english_version.note: No English text in the stored files, and a web search for MSIT English versions of the AI Basic Act guidelines found only law-firm and tracker summaries. The register's English title is the register's own rendering.

title.why: 'Guideline on Securing AI Transparency' renders 인공지능 투명성 확보 가이드라인 correctly (확보 = securing/ensuring). original_title matches the cover (PDF page 1) and the contents page (PDF page 3) character for character. The parenthetical '(Article 31 of the AI Basic Act)' is a register addition, not part of the title.

summary_claims.claim: It explains the three duties: prior notice to users that a product or service runs on high-impact or generative AI (para. 1); marking outputs as generated by generative AI (para. 2); and notice or marking of AI outputs that are hard to distinguish from reality, such as deepfakes, so that people can clearly recognise them (para. 3).
summary_claims.locator: PDF page 5, chapter 1 '투명성 확보 의무 내용'
summary_claims.original_quote: (제1항) 사전 고지 의무 (제2항) 표시 의무 (제3항) 딥페이크 생성물 표시 의무
summary_claims.literal_translation: (para. 1) prior-notice duty (para. 2) marking duty (para. 3) duty to mark deepfake outputs
summary_claims.note: The guideline treats 'deepfake' as the name for all para. 3 outputs and limits it to sound, image and video: 'Deepfake means virtual sound, image or video outputs that are hard to distinguish from reality; text is not included' (PDF page 9: '’딥페이크’란 “실제와 구분하기 어려운 가상의 음향, 이미지 또는 영상 등의 결과물”을 의미하며, 텍스트는 해당되지 않음'). 'Such as deepfakes' slightly blurs that definition.

summary_claims.claim: It sets out acceptable notice channels and marking methods (visible, audible or machine-readable) with service examples.
summary_claims.locator: PDF page 8 (chapter 2, decree Art. 23(2)); PDF pages 13 and 19-22 (export marking examples)
summary_claims.original_quote: 1. 표시 방법은 사람이 인식할 수 있는 방법과 기계가 판독할 수 있는 방법이 있음 2. 기계가 판독할 수 있는 방법을 사용할 경우에는 최소 1회 이상 안내 문구･음성 등을 제공해야 함
summary_claims.literal_translation: 1. Marking methods are methods humans can perceive and methods machines can read. 2. Where a machine-readable method is used, a notice text, voice message or similar must be given at least once.
summary_claims.note: 'Visible, audible' renders 'human-perceptible' (the audio examples speak of '가청적 방법', audible methods). Service examples (ChatGPT, Gemini, Firefly, voice assistants, games, productivity tools) are present.

summary_claims.claim: The ministry has said fines will not be imposed during a grace period of at least one year.
summary_claims.note: Neither the guideline nor the stored press-release page (headline and attachments only) mentions a grace period. The verification note says it rests on korea.kr policy news and press reports that were not stored.

key_terms.note: The KR-02 record renders the same duty as 'label'. Both are acceptable, but the register could use one term across the Korean records.

key_terms.original: 딥페이크 생성물 (실제와 구분하기 어려운 가상의 결과물)
key_terms.register_rendering: AI outputs that are hard to distinguish from reality, such as deepfakes
key_terms.note: In the guideline, 'deepfake' is the defined name for these outputs (sound, image, video; text excluded), not an example of them. The guideline also coins '일반 생성물' (general outputs) for everything else. Defensible, but not the guideline's structure.

issues: Summary: the grace-period sentence is not in any stored file (it rests on unstored press and policy news).

Notes understate the archive: they say press details on export marking, flexible in-service labelling and coverage of overseas providers 'were not checked against the full text', but the stored guideline contains all three (e.g. PDF page 6: '해외 사업자라도 우리 국민에게 영향을 미치면 적용 대상'; PDF page 13 on export marking). It also requires a human-perceptible mark for exported deepfakes ('사람이 직관적으로 인식할 수 있는 표시 방법 적용'), which the press-based wording 'visible or audible watermark or machine-readable metadata' blurs.
'Such as deepfakes' slightly misstates the guideline's definition: deepfake is its term for all para. 3 outputs, limited to sound, image and video.
Title carries a register-added parenthetical '(Article 31 of the AI Basic Act)'.
Not a translation issue: the cover names TTA (Telecommunications Technology Association) alongside MSIT; the issuing_body field names MSIT and NIA only.
note: The guideline also says the transparency duty falls on the operator that finally provides the AI product or service to users, not on a foundation-model developer that only supplies an API (PDF page 6). The summary does not say who is bound, so nothing contradicts this.
